krillion.quip: From Old French "grant merci" — once both a thank-you and a gasp of surprise.

quips.Gadzooks: A 1600s minced oath — basically polite cursing.
quips.Odds bodkins: A softened "God's body" — Elizabethans were masters of the minced oath.

krillion.quip: The orange-red of a wild poppy — it's simply the French word for poppy.

quips.Puce: French for "flea" — literally the colour of a flea.
quips.Eigengrau: German for "intrinsic grey" — what your eyes see in total darkness.
quips.Gamboge: A mustard-yellow tree resin, named after Cambodia.
quips.Glaucous: The dusty blue-grey bloom you can rub off a plum.

krillion.quip: Makes arrows — from Old French "flèche", meaning arrow.

quips.Cordwainer: A maker of new shoes — cobblers were only allowed to mend them.
quips.Knocker-upper: Before alarm clocks, they tapped on windows with long poles to wake workers.
quips.Tosher: Victorian scavengers who searched London's sewers for lost coins.
quips.Luthier: A maker of stringed instruments — from the French for lute.
quips.Fuller: Pounded wool cloth to thicken it, often by trampling it underfoot.

krillion.quip: From Persian "kamarband" — literally a loin-band.

chapters.text: Name a collective noun for a group of animals

krillion.quip: Like many of these, it was popularised by the 15th-century Book of Saint Albans.

quips.Bloat (of hippos): Hippos spend most of the day wallowing in water — bloat suits them.

quips.Silly Putty: A failed attempt at synthetic rubber that turned into a bestselling toy.

krillion.quip: A tiny drawstring handbag of Regency ladies — mocked at the time as a 'ridicule'.

quips.Sporran: The pouch worn with a kilt — because kilts have no pockets.

quips.Bum bag: Americans call it a fanny pack, a phrase that makes Brits blush.
quips.Carpetbag: Made from old carpet — and the origin of 'carpetbagger' in post-Civil War America.

krillion.quip: May live around 400 years, the longest-lived vertebrate known.

quips.Goblin shark: Its jaws shoot forward like a slingshot to snatch prey.
quips.Cookiecutter shark: Bites neat round plugs out of whales, dolphins and even submarine sonar domes.
quips.Epaulette shark: Can 'walk' across reefs on its fins and cope with very little oxygen.

krillion.quip: Nicknamed the werewolf cat for its patchy, wolfish coat, a natural mutation.

quips.Turkish Van: Nicknamed the swimming cat for its unusual love of water.
quips.Singapura: One of the smallest cat breeds, often weighing under 3 kg.
quips.Peterbald: A Russian breed that can be born bald, velvety or with a brush-like coat.

krillion.quip: Defends itself by blasting a boiling-hot chemical spray from its rear.

quips.Bullet ant: Its sting is often rated the most painful of any insect.
quips.Periodical cicada: Spends 13 or 17 years underground, then emerges in its millions all at once.
quips.Atlas moth: One of the largest moths, and the adults have no working mouth.

krillion.quip: Flattens its body into a ribbon to glide between treetops.

quips.Titanoboa: An extinct giant around 13 metres long, about the length of a bus.
quips.Inland taipan: The most venomous land snake known, yet it's shy and rarely bites.
quips.Tentacled snake: Uses two little face tentacles to sense fish in murky water.

krillion.quip: A tube-shaped cloud up to 1,000 km long that rolls over northern Australia.

quips.Ball lightning: Glowing orbs that drift through the air for seconds, still not fully explained.
quips.Snow roller: Wind rolls snow into hollow logs, like nature's own snowman starters.
quips.Thundersnow: A thunderstorm that drops snow instead of rain.

chapters.text: Name a mushroom or other fungus

krillion.quip: One in Oregon spreads across nearly 10 square km, among Earth's biggest organisms.

quips.Ghost fungus: Glows a soft green in the dark in Australian forests.
quips.Zombie-ant fungus: Hijacks an ant, steers it up a plant, then sprouts out of its head.
quips.Penicillium: The mould that gave us penicillin, the first widely used antibiotic.

krillion.quip: Its coat can have a natural metallic sheen that makes it look golden.

quips.Falabella: One of the smallest horse breeds, often under 80 cm at the shoulder.
quips.Icelandic horse: Has an extra smooth gait called the tölt, so riders barely bounce.
quips.Knabstrupper: A Danish breed famous for its leopard-spotted coat.

chapters.text: Name an animal native to Australia

krillion.quip: A striped termite-eater that can slurp up around 20,000 termites a day.

quips.Platypus: Lays eggs, has venomous ankle spurs and senses electricity with its bill.
quips.Lord Howe Island stick insect: Thought extinct for 80 years until found clinging to a lone sea stack.

krillion.quip: Looks half zebra, but it's actually the giraffe's only living relative.

quips.Aardwolf: A striped hyena relative that eats almost nothing but termites.
quips.Quagga: A half-striped zebra that went extinct in the 1880s.
quips.Thylacine: The striped 'Tasmanian tiger' was actually a carnivorous marsupial.

chapters.text: Name a whale, dolphin or porpoise

krillion.quip: The rarest marine mammal on Earth, with only about ten left in Mexico.

quips.Bowhead whale: Can live over 200 years, longer than any other known mammal.
quips.Narwhal: Its 'tusk' is really a long spiral tooth packed with nerve endings.
quips.Baiji: China's Yangtze river dolphin, declared likely extinct in 2006.

krillion.quip: Taps on wood, listens for grubs, then hooks them out with one skinny finger.

quips.Human: Yes, you count: humans are great apes, alongside chimps and gorillas.
quips.Slow loris: One of the few venomous primates, with a toxin gland on its elbow.
quips.Pygmy marmoset: The smallest monkey on Earth, light enough to perch on a finger.

krillion.quip: Lava from Earth's youth that erupted near 1,600°C, far hotter than any today.

quips.Pumice: So full of gas bubbles that it can float on water.
quips.Kimberlite: The volcanic rock that carries diamonds up from deep in the mantle.
quips.Chalk: Built from the tiny shells of countless ancient marine plankton.

krillion.quip: Gulps air at the surface and can grow to around 3 metres long.

quips.Electric eel: Not a true eel but a knifefish that can zap around 600 volts.
quips.Mekong giant catfish: One of the biggest freshwater fish, sometimes topping 250 kg.
quips.Bichir: An ancient fish with lungs that can wriggle across land on its fins.

krillion.quip: A blind cave salamander that can go up to a decade without eating.

quips.Glass frog: Its belly skin is see-through, so you can watch its heart beating.
quips.Darwin's frog: Dads raise tadpoles in their vocal sacs, then cough up tiny froglets.
quips.Hairy frog: Breaks its own toe bones to make claws when threatened.

krillion.quip: Discovered in 2005, it grows bacteria on its hairy arms near deep-sea vents.

quips.Coconut crab: The largest land invertebrate, strong enough to crack open coconuts.
quips.Mantis shrimp: Punches so fast it makes bubbles that collapse with a tiny flash of light.
quips.Tongue-eating louse: Replaces a fish's tongue and then lives on in its mouth.
quips.Japanese spider crab: Its legs can span nearly 4 metres from claw to claw.

packs.name: Science & Space
packs.tagline: 21 experiments · from atoms to galaxies

krillion.quip: The first element ever made artificially; its name is Greek for 'artificial'.

quips.Hafnium: Named after Copenhagen, whose old Latin name is Hafnia.
quips.Gallium: Melts in your hand: it turns liquid at about 30 °C.
quips.Oganesson: The heaviest element known, and only a handful of atoms have ever existed.

chapters.text: Name a bone in the human body

krillion.quip: A tiny wrist bone whose name literally means 'pea-shaped'.

quips.Hyoid: The only bone in your body not attached to any other bone.
quips.Stapes: The smallest bone in the body, shaped like a stirrup in your ear.
quips.Fabella: A little sesamoid bone behind the knee that only some people have.

chapters.text: Name a planet, dwarf planet or moon in our solar system

krillion.quip: A tiny Neptune moon found in old Hubble photos, named for a mythical sea-horse.

quips.Enceladus: Saturn's icy moon sprays water geysers into space from a hidden ocean.
quips.Titan: The only moon with a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane.
quips.Dactyl: The first moon ever found orbiting an asteroid, spotted by Galileo in 1993.

chapters.text: Name one of the 88 official constellations

krillion.quip: The giraffe: Greeks described it as a camel with leopard spots.

quips.Ophiuchus: The serpent bearer: the Sun passes through it, yet it never made the zodiac.
quips.Mensa: The table mountain, named after Table Mountain above Cape Town.
quips.Coma Berenices: Named after a real Egyptian queen's hair, offered to the gods.

chapters.text: Name an organ of the human body

krillion.quip: The fold holding your gut in place was only reclassified as an organ in 2016.

quips.Skin: Your biggest organ, weighing roughly as much as a bowling ball.
quips.Liver: The only internal organ that can regrow from just a quarter of itself.
quips.Appendix: Once called useless, it may store good gut bacteria for emergencies.

krillion.quip: Her pulsing-star rule gave astronomers their first ruler for measuring galaxies.

quips.Rosalind Franklin: Her X-ray Photo 51 revealed DNA's double helix shape.
quips.Mary Anning: A self-taught fossil hunter who found the first full ichthyosaur at about 12.
quips.Hypatia: A mathematician and astronomer who taught in Alexandria around 400 AD.

krillion.quip: An armoured ankylosaur named after the demon dog in Ghostbusters.

quips.Brontosaurus: Sunk as a mistake for a century, it was revived as a real genus in 2015.
quips.Yi: The shortest dinosaur name ever: a small bat-winged climber from China.
quips.Argentinosaurus: Possibly the heaviest land animal ever, at around 70 tonnes.

krillion.quip: MIT students measured a bridge using fellow student Oliver Smoot's body length.

quips.Barn: A tiny area used in nuclear physics; physicists joked a nucleus was as big as a barn.
quips.Shake: Ten nanoseconds, named after a 'shake of a lamb's tail'.
quips.Sverdrup: Measures ocean currents: one sverdrup is a million cubic metres of water per second.

krillion.quip: Its programs are abstract pixel paintings, named after the artist Piet Mondrian.

quips.Malbolge: Designed to be nearly impossible to program; its first 'Hello World' took two years.
quips.Plankalkül: Designed by Konrad Zuse in the 1940s, arguably the first high-level language.
quips.Whitespace: Only spaces, tabs and line breaks count; every other character is ignored.

chapters.text: Name a disease caused by a virus

krillion.quip: Studying this plant blight in the 1890s led scientists to discover viruses.

quips.Smallpox: The only human disease ever fully wiped out, declared eradicated in 1980.
quips.Rinderpest: A cattle plague that became only the second disease ever eradicated, in 2011.
quips.Myxomatosis: Deliberately released in Australia in 1950 to control rabbit numbers.

krillion.quip: Added to the cloud atlas in 2017 after amateur sky-watchers campaigned for it.

quips.Morning Glory: A huge rolling tube cloud that sweeps over northern Australia each spring.
quips.Noctilucent: The highest clouds on Earth, glowing at night about 80 km up.
quips.Virga: Rain that evaporates before it reaches the ground, like wispy streaks.

chapters.text: Name a branch of science ending in -ology

krillion.quip: The scientific study of clouds, from the Greek 'nephos', meaning cloud.

quips.Oology: The study of birds' eggs, once a hugely popular Victorian hobby.
quips.Areology: Geology, but for Mars: named after Ares, the Greek god of war.
quips.Dendrochronology: Dating events by counting and comparing tree rings.

krillion.quip: The fear of peanut butter sticking to the roof of your mouth.

quips.Hippopotomonstrosesquippedaliophobia: The fear of long words, cruelly given one of the longest names possible.
quips.Nomophobia: Fear of being without your phone, short for 'no-mobile-phone phobia'.

chapters.text: Name a famous space mission or spacecraft

krillion.quip: Lost in 1999 because one team used pound-force and the other used newtons.

quips.Voyager 1: The farthest human-made object, now cruising through interstellar space.
quips.Ingenuity: The first aircraft to make a powered, controlled flight on another planet.
quips.Luna 9: The first spacecraft to soft-land on the Moon, in 1966.

krillion.quip: A real London phone maker founded by Carl Pei, so 'Nothing' scores here.

quips.Fairchild Semiconductor: Its founders spun off so many startups they became known as the 'Fairchildren'.
quips.Nokia: Started in 1865 as a paper mill in Finland before it ever made phones.
quips.Nintendo: Founded in 1889 to make hand-made playing cards.

chapters.text: Name an invention of the 20th century

krillion.quip: Percy Shaw got the idea for reflective road studs from a cat's glowing eyes.

quips.Velcro: Inspired by burrs that clung to George de Mestral's dog after a walk in the Alps.
quips.Microwave oven: Discovered when radar engineer Percy Spencer noticed a chocolate bar melting in his pocket.
quips.Bubble wrap: Originally sold as textured wallpaper, which flopped.

chapters.text: Name a muscle in the human body

krillion.quip: Your smallest skeletal muscle, steadying the tiniest bone deep in your ear.

quips.Sartorius: The longest muscle in the body, named after tailors who sat cross-legged.
quips.Palmaris longus: Missing from one or both arms in about one person in seven.
quips.Masseter: Pound for pound, one of the strongest muscles you have: it powers your bite.

krillion.quip: Found in Serbia in 2006 with almost the exact formula of Superman's kryptonite.

quips.Bridgmanite: Earth's most abundant mineral, hidden in the deep mantle and only named in 2014.
quips.Ice: Yes, ice counts: it is naturally occurring, crystalline and inorganic.
quips.Painite: Once the rarest gem on Earth, with fewer than two dozen crystals known in the 2000s.

krillion.quip: A convex 3D shape with one stable resting point; it always rolls itself upright.

quips.Reuleaux triangle: A curved triangle of constant width; it can drill nearly square holes.
quips.Apeirogon: A polygon with infinitely many sides.
quips.Szilassi polyhedron: Seven faces, and every single face touches every other one.

chapters.text: Name a star other than the Sun

krillion.quip: Spotted in 2022 about 12.9 billion years back in time: the most distant single star seen.

quips.Polaris: Not the brightest star, but it sits almost exactly above Earth's North Pole.
quips.Keid: The real star Star Trek picked for Spock's home planet, Vulcan.
quips.Algol: The 'Demon Star' visibly dims every three days as its partner star eclipses it.

chapters.text: Name a piece of science lab equipment

krillion.quip: A three-bulb glass gadget that makes gas on demand and stops when you shut the tap.

quips.Bunsen burner: Popularised by Robert Bunsen in 1855, though his technician did much of the design.
quips.Petri dish: Named after Julius Petri, an assistant to germ pioneer Robert Koch.
quips.Leyden jar: One of the first devices to store electricity, invented in the 1740s.

packs.name: Body & Health
packs.tagline: 21 check-ups · the doctor will see you now

chapters.text: Name a part of the face

krillion.quip: The groove above your upper lip — its name comes from the Greek for 'love charm'.

quips.Glabella: The smooth patch between your eyebrows — doctors tap it to test a reflex.
quips.Cupid's bow: The double curve of your upper lip, named after the archer god's weapon.
quips.Buccinator: The cheek muscle trumpeters rely on — its name comes from the Latin for trumpeter.

chapters.text: Name a type of doctor or medical specialty

krillion.quip: A rehab-medicine doctor — not a psychiatrist, and definitely not a podiatrist.

quips.Veterinarian: Vets train on many species — a GP for humans only has to learn one.
quips.Optometrist: An eye-exam specialist; ophthalmologists are the ones who do eye surgery.
quips.Podiatrist: A foot specialist — the name comes from the Greek for 'foot' and 'healer'.

chapters.text: Name a vitamin or dietary mineral

krillion.quip: You need only a pinch, but it powers enzymes that break down sulfites.

quips.Vitamin C: Humans are among the few mammals that can't make their own vitamin C.
quips.Vitamin D: Your skin makes it from sunlight, which is why it's nicknamed the sunshine vitamin.
quips.Cobalt: It sits at the heart of the vitamin B12 molecule — the only vitamin with a metal core.

chapters.text: Name a gym or bodyweight exercise

krillion.quip: Bruce Lee's signature core move — your whole body levers up off a bench like a flag.

quips.Burpee: Named after physiologist Royal Burpee, who invented it in the 1930s as a fitness test.
quips.Jumping jack: Legend credits US Army general John 'Black Jack' Pershing with popularising it.
quips.Planche: A gymnast's hold where your whole body hovers flat, balanced only on your hands.

chapters.text: Name something you'd find in a first-aid kit

krillion.quip: A tiny hooked tool that twists ticks out cleanly — a staple of hikers' kits.

quips.Plaster: The Band-Aid was invented in 1920 by a Johnson & Johnson employee for his accident-prone wife.
quips.Triangular bandage: One cloth, a dozen uses: sling, pad, tie or even a makeshift tourniquet.

chapters.text: Name a part of the human eye

krillion.quip: The pink fold in your eye's inner corner — a leftover of a third eyelid.

quips.Cornea: It has no blood vessels at all — it takes its oxygen straight from the air.
quips.Optic disc: No photoreceptors sit here, so your brain quietly paints over the blind spot.
quips.Dua's layer: A thin layer of the cornea first described only in 2013.

chapters.text: Name a sleep disorder or something that can happen in your sleep

krillion.quip: Sleep groaning: long, eerie moans on each out-breath that the sleeper never hears.

quips.Narcolepsy: Some people with it collapse when they laugh, as strong emotions switch their muscles off.
quips.Exploding head syndrome: A harmless but startling 'bang' heard as you drift off — no headache involved.
quips.Hypnic jerk: That falling-feeling twitch as you drop off — most people get one now and then.

chapters.text: Name a hormone in the human body

krillion.quip: Named after Hershey's Kisses — it was discovered in Hershey, Pennsylvania.

quips.Oxytocin: Nicknamed the 'cuddle hormone' — it's released during hugs and childbirth.
quips.Ghrelin: Your 'hunger hormone': levels climb before meals and fall once you've eaten.
quips.Melatonin: Your body releases it as darkness falls, nudging you toward sleep.
quips.Irisin: Released by exercising muscle, it's named after Iris, the Greek messenger goddess.

chapters.text: Name a part of the brain

krillion.quip: Latin for 'tree of life' — the branching white matter inside your cerebellum.

deepcut: Bed nucleus of the stria terminalis

quips.Hippocampus: Named after the seahorse, which early anatomists thought it resembled.
quips.Amygdala: From the Greek for 'almond' — it's an almond-shaped hub for fear and emotion.
quips.Claustrum: A thin sheet of neurons that Francis Crick suspected might help bind consciousness.
quips.Pineal gland: Descartes called it the seat of the soul; it actually makes melatonin.

chapters.text: Name a joint in the human body (or a type of joint)

krillion.quip: The peg-in-socket joint that anchors each of your teeth in the jaw.

quips.Saddle joint: Your thumb's base sits in a saddle joint — the secret behind gripping with opposable thumbs.
quips.Pubic symphysis: It loosens during pregnancy, helped along by the hormone relaxin.
quips.Suture: Skull bones meet at wiggly suture joints that fuse slowly as you age.

chapters.text: Name a piece of medical equipment or a medical instrument

krillion.quip: A trumpet-shaped tube midwives press to the bump to hear a baby's heartbeat.

quips.Stethoscope: Invented in 1816 by René Laennec, whose first version was a rolled-up tube of paper.
quips.Iron lung: A whole-body breathing chamber that saved thousands during the polio epidemics.
quips.Defibrillator: It doesn't restart a stopped heart — it resets one that's quivering out of rhythm.

krillion.quip: A sudden calf-muscle tear named after the sport where lunging so often causes it.

quips.Tennis elbow: Most people who get tennis elbow have never picked up a racket.
quips.Cauliflower ear: Blood pools under the ear's skin after repeated blows and hardens into bumps.
quips.Turf toe: A big-toe sprain that became common once American football moved onto artificial turf.

chapters.text: Name a part of the ear

krillion.quip: A small bump on some people's ear rim that Darwin wrote about as an evolutionary leftover.

quips.Stapes: The smallest bone in your body — about the size of a grain of rice.
quips.Otoliths: Tiny calcium crystals in your inner ear that tell your brain which way is down.
quips.Tragus: The little flap in front of your ear canal — press it to muffle sound.

chapters.text: Name a nerve in the human body

krillion.quip: A tiny vagus branch nicknamed 'criminal' for letting ulcers return after surgery.

deepcut: Medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm
Lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm
Medial cutaneous nerve of the arm
Dorsal cutaneous branch of the ulnar nerve

Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh
Posterior femoral cutaneous nerve: Posterior cutaneous nerve of the thigh
Arnold's nerve: Auricular branch of the vagus nerve
Superficial radial nerve: Superficial branch of the radial nerve

quips.Ulnar nerve: Hitting your 'funny bone' is really whacking this exposed nerve at the elbow.
quips.Vagus nerve: Its name means 'wandering' — it meanders from your brainstem all the way to your gut.
quips.Sciatic nerve: The longest and widest nerve in your body — about as thick as your thumb at its widest.
quips.Terminal nerve: Sometimes called 'cranial nerve zero', it was discovered after the other twelve were numbered.

chapters.text: Name a gland in the human body

krillion.quip: Tiny glands at the back of your tongue that rinse your taste buds clean between bites.

quips.Liver: The body's largest gland as well as its largest internal organ.
quips.Pineal gland: It's shaped like a tiny pine cone, which is how it got its name.
quips.Thymus: It trains your T cells, then slowly shrinks and turns to fat after puberty.

chapters.text: Name a type of cell in the human body

krillion.quip: Brain cells that fire when you're in one particular spot — your built-in GPS.

quips.Red blood cell: They ditch their nucleus as they mature, leaving more room for oxygen-carrying haemoglobin.
quips.Egg cell: The largest cell in the human body — just about visible to the naked eye.
quips.Osteoclast: A bone-dissolving cell that constantly remodels your skeleton.
quips.Grid cell: Neurons that fire in a hexagonal grid pattern as you move around — Nobel-winning stuff.

chapters.text: Name a reflex or involuntary body action

krillion.quip: Poking inside your ear makes some people cough, thanks to a branch of the vagus nerve.

quips.Yawn: Yawning is contagious — even reading about it can set you off.
quips.Photic sneeze reflex: Bright light makes roughly one in four people sneeze — it's nicknamed ACHOO syndrome.
quips.Diving reflex: Cold water on your face slows your heart — a built-in trick for holding your breath.

chapters.text: Name a part of the hand or foot

krillion.quip: The hollow at the base of your thumb, named for where people once rested a pinch of snuff.

deepcut: Ulnar collateral ligament of the thumb

quips.Lunula: The pale half-moon at the base of your nail — its name is Latin for 'little moon'.
quips.Fingerprint: Even identical twins have different fingerprints.
quips.Pisiform: The pea-shaped wrist bone sits inside a tendon, just as your kneecap does.

chapters.text: Name a medical test or scan

krillion.quip: A paper strip hooked under your lower eyelid measures how many tears you make.

quips.X-ray: Wilhelm Röntgen's first X-ray photo showed his wife's hand — wedding ring and all.
quips.Heel prick test: A few drops from a newborn's heel can screen for several rare but treatable conditions.
quips.Pap smear: Named after Georgios Papanikolaou, the Greek doctor who developed it.

chapters.text: Name a medicine (generic or brand name)

krillion.quip: A heart drug made from foxglove, a plant whose heart effects were described back in 1785.

quips.Penicillin: Alexander Fleming spotted it in 1928 when mould spoiled one of his bacteria dishes.
quips.Aspirin: Its ancestor, salicin, comes from willow bark — used for pain since ancient times.
quips.Quinine: Extracted from cinchona bark, it's what gives tonic water its bitter bite.

chapters.text: Name an artery or vein in the human body

krillion.quip: A deep brain vein named after Galen, the Roman-era Greek doctor who dissected apes.

quips.Aorta: Your body's biggest artery — at its start it's about as wide as a garden hose.
quips.Great saphenous vein: The longest vein in your body, running from the top of your foot to your groin.
quips.Pulmonary artery: Unlike most arteries, they carry oxygen-poor blood — from the heart to the lungs.

packs.name: History & Myth
packs.tagline: 21 relics · dust off the old stories

krillion.quip: The first president born a US citizen — and he grew up speaking Dutch.

quips.William Henry Harrison: He served just 31 days — the shortest presidency ever.
quips.Grover Cleveland: For over a century the only president with two non-consecutive terms.

chapters.text: Name a Greek god or goddess

krillion.quip: Primordial goddess of night — Homer says even Zeus feared to anger her.

quips.Hecate: Goddess of crossroads and witchcraft, often shown with three faces.
quips.Nike: Goddess of victory — the sportswear brand borrowed her name.
quips.Momus: God of mockery, so critical the gods threw him out of Olympus.

krillion.quip: Painted abstract art before Kandinsky, but asked that it stay hidden for decades.

quips.Bob Ross: Painted over 30,000 canvases and never once lost his calm.
quips.Raphael: Died at 37, yet ranks with Leonardo and Michelangelo in the Renaissance trinity.

krillion.quip: Co-written with John Fletcher and based on Chaucer's The Knight's Tale.

Edward III: The Reign of King Edward the Third

quips.Edward III: Only accepted into the Shakespeare canon in the 1990s.
quips.Titus Andronicus: His bloodiest play — two villains end up baked into a pie.

krillion.quip: He bought the throne at auction from the Praetorian Guard in AD 193.

quips.Caligula: Ancient gossip claims he planned to make his horse Incitatus a consul.
quips.Romulus Augustulus: The last Western emperor, deposed as a teenager in AD 476.
quips.Constantine XI Palaiologos: The last Byzantine emperor, killed defending Constantinople in 1453.

krillion.quip: A Bavarian horned, winged rabbit — taxidermists still stitch together 'specimens'.

quips.Bunyip: An Australian swamp monster said to lurk in billabongs and waterholes.
quips.Tarasque: A Provençal dragon-turtle, tamed in legend by Saint Martha.
quips.Kappa: Japanese water imp — bow to it, and it bows back, spilling its powers.

krillion.quip: A Greek from Marseille who sailed to Britain c. 325 BC and wrote of distant 'Thule'.

rare: René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle

quips.Leif Erikson: Reached North America around 1000 AD, nearly 500 years before Columbus.
quips.Matthew Henson: Peary's African American partner on the famous 1909 North Pole expedition.

chapters.text: Name an English or British monarch

krillion.quip: King of England who collapsed and died mid-toast at a wedding feast in 1042.

quips.Lady Jane Grey: Queen for just nine days in 1553 before Mary I took the throne.
quips.Edward VIII: Abdicated after less than a year to marry Wallis Simpson.
quips.Athelstan: Usually counted as the first King of all England, from 927.

chapters.text: Name a Norse god or goddess

krillion.quip: Odin's son who rode Sleipnir down to Hel to beg for Baldur's return.

quips.Hel: Loki's daughter, ruler of the dead — half her body was said to be blue-black.
quips.Bragi: God of poetry, said to have runes carved on his tongue.
quips.Kvasir: So wise that, after his murder, his blood was brewed into the mead of poetry.

krillion.quip: Saharan farmers who tapped hidden groundwater with long tunnels called foggaras.

quips.Norte Chico: Built pyramids in Peru around the same era as Egypt's first pyramids.
quips.Minoans: Bronze Age Cretans famous for bull-leaping frescoes at Knossos.

krillion.quip: In 751 the Abbasids beat Tang China; legend says captive papermakers took paper west.

rare: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
Battle of the Plains of Abraham

quips.Battle of Thermopylae: 300 Spartans and several thousand other Greeks held the pass for three days.
quips.Battle of Hastings: 1066 — Harold II was killed, traditionally by an arrow to the eye.
quips.Battle of Rorke's Drift: About 150 defenders held off thousands; eleven Victoria Crosses followed.

krillion.quip: A Cynic who married Crates and lived on the streets of Athens as his equal.

quips.Diogenes: Lived in a large jar and told Alexander the Great to stop blocking his sun.
quips.Thales: Often called the first philosopher; he reportedly predicted a solar eclipse.

chapters.text: Name an ancient Egyptian god or goddess

krillion.quip: An obscure 'smiter' from the Book of the Dead, drawn like a sheet-ghost with eyes.

quips.Bes: A dwarf god who protected households, mothers and children from evil.
quips.Taweret: Part hippo, part crocodile, part lion — and the guardian of childbirth.
quips.Apep: Giant serpent of chaos who attacked Ra's sun boat every night.

chapters.text: Name a hero of Greek mythology

krillion.quip: Amazon queen at Troy — Achilles killed her, then fell for her as she died.

quips.Bellerophon: Tamed Pegasus to slay the Chimera, then flew too high and was thrown.
quips.Atalanta: A huntress who lost a footrace only because she stopped for golden apples.

chapters.text: Name a knight of the Round Table

krillion.quip: King Arthur's court jester, knighted as a joke — yet he took a seat at the Table.

Ironside: Red Knight of the Red Lands

quips.Galahad: The purest knight, and the one who finally achieved the Holy Grail.
quips.Mordred: Arthur's nephew (or son) whose rebellion ended Camelot at Camlann.

chapters.text: Name a Nobel Peace Prize laureate

krillion.quip: An agronomist whose high-yield wheat is credited with saving up to a billion lives.

schooler: International Committee of the Red Cross

krillion.quip: The widowed field mouse who asks the clever rats of NIMH to help move her home.

quips.Winnie-the-Pooh: Named for Winnipeg, a real Canadian black bear that lived at London Zoo.
quips.Peter Pan: Barrie signed over the play's rights to Great Ormond Street Hospital for sick children.
quips.Paddington Bear: Michael Bond spotted a lone toy bear on a London shop shelf on Christmas Eve, 1956.

packs.name: Cars & Transport
packs.tagline: 21 journeys · are we there yet?

krillion.quip: Trabants had Duroplast bodies made from resin and recycled cotton waste.

quips.Isetta: The Isetta's entire front end swung open as the door, steering wheel and all.
quips.Peel P50: The Peel P50 holds the record for smallest production car ever made.
quips.Model T: Ford sold over 15 million Model Ts between 1908 and 1927.
quips.Countach: Countach drivers famously reversed by perching on the sill with the scissor door up.

chapters.text: Name a type of car (body style or category)

krillion.quip: Shooting brakes began as horse-drawn wagons carrying hunting parties and their guns.

quips.Fastback: The Ford Mustang made the fastback roofline a pop-culture icon.
quips.Kei car: Japan's kei cars are limited to 660 cc engines and a tiny footprint.
quips.Gull-wing: The 1954 Mercedes 300 SL's gull-wing doors were needed because of its tubular frame.

krillion.quip: Curiosity's wheel treads stamp 'JPL' in Morse code into the Martian dust.

quips.Zamboni: Frank Zamboni built the first ice resurfacer in 1949 for his California rink.
quips.Lunar rover: Apollo's lunar rover folded up and rode to the Moon bolted to the side of the lander.

krillion.quip: Loganair's Westray to Papa Westray hop is the world's shortest scheduled flight.

quips.Pan Am: Pan Am's Clipper flying boats linked California to Asia in the 1930s.
quips.Laker Airways: Freddie Laker's cut-price Skytrain helped invent cheap transatlantic flying.
quips.Qantas: Qantas was founded in 1920 as the Queensland and Northern Territory Aerial Services.

krillion.quip: At Princess Juliana, jets skim Maho Beach so low that sunbathers feel the blast.

quips.Kai Tak: Kai Tak's approach had pilots banking low over Hong Kong rooftops to line up the runway.
quips.Tempelhof: Tempelhof's 1930s terminal was once among the largest buildings in the world.
quips.Heathrow: Heathrow began in 1929 as a small airfield called the Great West Aerodrome.

chapters.text: Name a type of boat or ship

krillion.quip: A coracle is so light and round that one person can carry it on their back.

quips.Currach: Irish currachs are made of tarred canvas stretched over a wooden frame, once animal hide.
quips.Hovercraft: Christopher Cockerell tested his hovercraft idea using a cat-food tin and a vacuum cleaner.
quips.Dromon: Dromons were the Byzantine navy's main warships, famous for hurling Greek fire.

chapters.text: Name a part of a ship

krillion.quip: Said 'gunnel': it began as the plank that supported a warship's guns.

quips.Plimsoll line: Samuel Plimsoll campaigned for the load line that curbed overloaded 'coffin ships'.
quips.Binnacle: The binnacle is the stand that holds a ship's compass, often with a built-in lamp.
quips.Poop deck: It comes from the Latin puppis, meaning stern, and not from anything rude.

krillion.quip: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, died riding his Brough Superior in 1935.

quips.Hildebrand & Wolfmüller: Their 1894 machine is regarded as the first production motorcycle.
quips.Britten: John Britten hand-built his radical V1000 superbike in a New Zealand workshop.
quips.Vincent: Vincent's Black Lightning set motorcycle speed records on the salt flats in 1948.
quips.Hesketh: Lord Hesketh also ran a Formula One team, with a young James Hunt driving.

chapters.text: Name a type of aircraft (not a specific model)

krillion.quip: An autogyro's rotor spins freely in the airflow while a propeller pulls it forward.

quips.Ornithopter: Ornithopters flap their wings like birds; Leonardo da Vinci sketched one in the 1480s.
quips.Rozière balloon: A Rozière balloon pairs hydrogen with hot air; it killed its inventor, Pilâtre de Rozier.
quips.Flying wing: Flying wings drop the tail and fuselage entirely; the B-2 stealth bomber is one.

chapters.text: Name a famous train or railway

krillion.quip: The Darjeeling 'Toy Train' runs on 2-foot gauge track and is a World Heritage Site.

quips.Jupiter: Jupiter met Union Pacific's No. 119 nose to nose at Promontory Summit in 1869.
quips.Tren Maya: Mexico's Tren Maya loops around the Yucatan Peninsula past Chichen Itza.
quips.Rocket: Stephenson's Rocket won the 1829 Rainhill Trials at about 30 miles per hour.

chapters.text: Name a part of a car

krillion.quip: A Panhard rod stops an axle sliding sideways; it's named for the French maker Panhard.

quips.Differential: A differential lets the outer wheel spin faster than the inner one in a turn.
quips.Crumple zone: Béla Barényi, a Mercedes engineer, patented the crumple zone in 1952.
quips.Bonnet ornament: Rolls-Royce's flying lady mascot was modelled on Eleanor Thornton.

chapters.text: Name a city with a metro or subway system

krillion.quip: Tashkent opened Central Asia's first metro in 1977, with stations decorated like palaces.

quips.Budapest: Budapest's Line 1 opened in 1896, the first underground railway on mainland Europe.
quips.Glasgow: The Glasgow Subway's nickname is the Clockwork Orange, for its orange trains.
quips.Pyongyang: Pyongyang's metro stations are among the deepest in the world, and ornately decorated.
quips.Haifa: Haifa's Carmelit is a funicular and counts as Israel's only subway.

krillion.quip: The 1817 draisine had no pedals; riders pushed along the ground with their feet.

quips.Penny-farthing: The big wheel of a penny-farthing meant a bigger gear, but a longer fall.
quips.Velomobile: A velomobile is a pedal-powered recumbent trike wrapped in an aerodynamic shell.
quips.Boneshaker: Boneshakers had iron-rimmed wooden wheels, hence the name.

krillion.quip: Brooklands, opened in 1907, was the world's first purpose-built motor racing circuit.

Imola: Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari Imola

quips.Brooklands: Brooklands' banked concrete oval was built in 1907 near Weybridge, Surrey.
quips.Targa Florio: The Targa Florio ran on Sicilian mountain roads from 1906 and was one of motorsport's oldest races.
quips.Pikes Peak: Pikes Peak's hill climb has run to a 14,000-foot summit since 1916.
quips.Nürburgring: Jackie Stewart nicknamed the Nordschleife 'the Green Hell'.

krillion.quip: Slow, fabric-covered Swordfish biplanes crippled the Bismarck's rudder in 1941.

quips.Fairey Swordfish: Despite its antique look, the Swordfish sank more Axis shipping than any other British aircraft.
quips.XB-70 Valkyrie: The XB-70 flew at Mach 3 by riding its own shockwave under folding wingtips.
quips.Avro Arrow: Canada scrapped its Mach 2 Avro Arrow interceptor in 1959, and the debate still rages.
quips.Fokker Dr.I: Manfred von Richthofen, the Red Baron, scored his last victories in a Fokker Dr.I.

chapters.text: Name a space rocket or launch vehicle

krillion.quip: Britain's Black Arrow put the Prospero satellite in orbit in 1971, then was cancelled.

quips.Black Arrow: Britain remains the only nation to have orbited a satellite and then dropped its rocket programme.
quips.V-2: In 1944 a V-2 became the first human-made object to reach space on a suborbital flight.
quips.N1: The Soviet N1 Moon rocket never reached orbit; all four test launches failed.
quips.Starship: Starship is the tallest and most powerful rocket ever launched.

krillion.quip: A droshky is a light open Russian cab, drawn by horses around old St Petersburg.

Surrey: Surrey with the fringe on top

quips.Shooting brake: Before it described a car body, a shooting brake carried hunters and their guns by horse.
quips.Hansom cab: Joseph Hansom patented the cab in 1834; the driver sat on a perch behind.
quips.Gold State Coach: The Gold State Coach has carried every British monarch to their coronation since 1831.

chapters.text: Name a famous car from the movies or television

krillion.quip: The Blues Brothers' Bluesmobile is an ex-police 1974 Dodge Monaco.

Bandit's Trans Am: Smokey and the Bandit Trans Am
Bond's AMC Hornet: Man with the Golden Gun AMC Hornet

quips.Bluesmobile: Elwood bought the old cop car at auction, and the brothers were on a mission from God.
quips.DeLorean: The real DeLorean DMC-12 had a stainless-steel body and gull-wing doors.
quips.Pursuit Special: The Pursuit Special was a customised Australian Ford Falcon XB GT Coupe.
quips.Mr. Bean's Mini: Mr. Bean's lime-green Mini was a 1976 Leyland Mini 1000.

chapters.text: Name a vehicle or machine you'd see on a building site

krillion.quip: Skid steers turn by braking one side's wheels, so they spin on the spot.

quips.Skid steer: The first skid-steer loader was built in 1957 by the Keller brothers in North Dakota.
quips.Franna crane: Franna cranes pick up a load and then drive with it, a trick called pick-and-carry.
quips.Tunnel boring machine: Tunnel boring machines are usually lowered in pieces and assembled in a shaft.
quips.Telehandler: A telehandler is a forklift with a telescopic boom that can reach over walls.

krillion.quip: The Citroën Ami is a tiny electric quadricycle you can drive from age 14 in France.

quips.Citroën Ami: The Ami tops out at 45 km/h, which is why 14-year-olds can drive it in France.
quips.GM EV1: General Motors leased the EV1 in the 1990s, then famously reclaimed and crushed most.
quips.Sinclair C5: Sir Clive Sinclair's 1985 C5 was an electric trike with a top speed of 15 mph.
quips.Rimac Nevera: The Rimac Nevera hit 60 mph in under two seconds and set a string of EV records.

chapters.text: Name a model of passenger airliner

krillion.quip: The Soviet Tu-144 flew supersonic two months before Concorde, on 31 December 1968.

Twin Otter: De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter

quips.Tupolev Tu-144: The Tu-144 was nicknamed Concordski, but a 1973 Paris Air Show crash dented its career.
quips.Boeing 314 Clipper: Pan Am's Boeing 314 Clipper flying boats crossed the Atlantic and Pacific in the late 1930s.
quips.Boeing 747: The 747's upper-deck hump was designed so its nose could swing open as a freighter.
quips.Concorde: Concorde cruised at Mach 2 and flew London to New York in about three and a half hours.

packs.name: Home & Hobbies
packs.tagline: 21 weekends · find a new obsession

krillion.quip: Mudlarkers comb the Thames foreshore at low tide for centuries-old lost treasures.

quips.Geocaching: A worldwide treasure hunt: you use GPS to find hidden containers called caches.
quips.Pigeon racing: Racing pigeons can find their way home from hundreds of miles away.
quips.Kendama: A Japanese cup-and-ball skill toy with competitions around the world.
quips.Pinball: Early pinball machines had no flippers at all, so skill was nearly impossible.

chapters.text: Name something you'd find in a toolbox

krillion.quip: A weight on a string — builders have used it to find true vertical for millennia.

quips.Spokeshave: A woodworker's two-handled blade for shaping curves like chair legs and wheel spokes.
quips.Bradawl: A small pointed tool that starts screw holes in wood without splitting it.
quips.Feeler gauge: A fan of thin steel strips used to measure tiny gaps, such as in engines.
quips.Vice grips: The original Vise-Grip was invented in 1924 by William Petersen of Nebraska.

krillion.quip: Japanese 'floating ink' marbling, with roots reaching back to around the 12th century.

quips.Kintsugi: Japanese artisans mend broken pottery with gold, so the cracks become the feature.
quips.Pysanky: Ukrainian eggs are decorated with wax-resist designs, layer by layer, in rich dyes.
quips.Origami: Origami comes from the Japanese 'ori' (folding) and 'kami' (paper).
quips.Furoshiki: Furoshiki is the Japanese art of wrapping gifts and goods in a square of cloth.

chapters.text: Name a dance or dance style

krillion.quip: Filipino dancers hop between clacking bamboo poles, imitating the tikling bird.

quips.Haka: The haka is a Māori ceremonial dance, famously performed by New Zealand's All Blacks.
quips.Moonwalk: Michael Jackson unveiled it on TV in 1983, though others had glided backwards before him.
quips.Can-can: The can-can first shocked audiences in 1830s Paris music halls.
quips.Capoeira: Capoeira, an Afro-Brazilian art, blends dance, acrobatics and fighting set to music.
quips.Kecak: Bali's kecak has a huge circle of men chanting 'cak' instead of using instruments.

krillion.quip: A decorative woven ring that sailors wrap around rails, handles and ship's wheels.

rare: Round turn and two half hitches

quips.Monkey's fist: Sailors tie it round a ball so a light line can be thrown a long way.
quips.Prusik knot: Climbers use it to slide up or lock onto a rope; it's named after Karl Prusik.
quips.Bimini twist: An anglers' knot that creates a doubled line, said to keep nearly full line strength.
quips.Zeppelin bend: Strong, yet easy to untie even after heavy loading.

krillion.quip: Lithops, the 'living stones', mimic pebbles to hide from hungry animals.

quips.Venus flytrap: A flytrap snaps shut only after two touches within about 20 seconds, saving energy.
quips.Ponytail palm: Not a true palm: it stores water in its swollen trunk base like a succulent.
quips.Spider plant: Spider plants grow dangling baby plantlets that you can simply snip off and pot up.
quips.Mother of thousands: It sprouts hundreds of tiny plantlets along its leaf edges, ready to drop and root.
quips.Lucky bamboo: Despite the name, lucky bamboo is a Dracaena, not a true bamboo.

krillion.quip: This Japanese digging knife is named by saying the word for 'dig' twice.

quips.Dibber: A pointed wooden peg that makes the perfect hole for seedlings and bulbs.
quips.Scythe: Scythes have been used to cut grass and harvest grain for well over a thousand years.
quips.Billhook: A hooked blade used for hedge laying and trimming small branches.
quips.Strimmer: The weed trimmer was invented in the 1970s by George Ballas, inspired by car-wash brushes.

krillion.quip: A clamp that presses a crease into trousers overnight — still a hotel-room classic.

quips.Mangle: Victorian mangles squeezed water out of laundry between two heavy rollers.
quips.Samovar: A samovar is a traditional Russian urn that keeps water hot for tea.
quips.Microwave: The microwave oven was invented after a candy bar melted in a radar engineer's pocket.
quips.Twin tub: A twin tub has separate drums for washing and spinning, so you move the clothes yourself.

krillion.quip: Australian campers boil their tea in this tin pot, called a 'billy'.

quips.Billycan: The word 'billy' for a bush kettle goes back to 19th-century Australia.
quips.Ferro rod: A ferrocerium rod throws sparks around 3,000°C, even when it is wet.
quips.Marshmallows: Marshmallows were first made from the root sap of the marshmallow plant.
quips.Hammock: Hammock camping keeps you off wet, lumpy ground, if you can find two good trees.

krillion.quip: Also called Picross, Griddlers or Hanjie — number clues reveal a hidden picture.

quips.Tangram: Tangram's seven flat pieces can be arranged into thousands of different shapes.
quips.Seven Bridges of Königsberg: Euler's 1736 solution to this puzzle founded graph theory.
quips.Tower of Hanoi: Solving it with n discs takes at least 2^n minus 1 moves.
quips.Rubik's Cube: Erno Rubik invented the Cube in 1974 as a teaching tool for his architecture students.

chapters.text: Name something you'd find in a playground

krillion.quip: Spring riders are the bouncy animals on a coil, also called spring rockers.

quips.Seesaw: Seesaw physics: a lighter child sits farther from the pivot to balance a heavier one.
quips.Monkey bars: Brachiating, swinging hand over hand, is how gibbons travel through the trees.
quips.Hopscotch: Hopscotch is said to date to ancient Rome, where children copied soldiers' drills.

chapters.text: Name a fishing term or piece of fishing gear

krillion.quip: In Scotland a ghillie guides anglers on the river, helping them find and land fish.

quips.Tippet: Fly anglers tie a fine, nearly invisible tippet between the leader and the fly.
quips.Berley: Berley is what Australians call the chopped bait thrown out to attract fish.
quips.Spey casting: Spey casting takes its name from Scotland's River Spey.

krillion.quip: Hide-and-seek in reverse: one person hides and everyone else squeezes in with them.

plankton: Pin the tail on the donkey

I spy: I spy with my little eye

quips.Sardines: Sardines is hide-and-seek in reverse: everyone ends up crammed into one hiding place.
quips.Charades: Charades began as a 1700s French parlour game acted out in rhyme or riddle form.
quips.Pass the parcel: In pass the parcel, each unwrapped layer of paper might hide a small prize.
quips.Limbo: Limbo comes from Trinidad, where it began as a wake ritual.

krillion.quip: A rainforest relative of the raccoon with a very long tongue, nicknamed 'honey bear'.

quips.Axolotl: Axolotls can regrow lost limbs, and even parts of their hearts and brains.
quips.Fennec fox: A fennec's huge ears help it shed heat in the Sahara.
quips.Sugar glider: Sugar gliders can glide up to about 50 metres between trees on a skin membrane.
quips.Pet rock: Gary Dahl sold over a million Pet Rocks in 1975, complete with a training manual.
quips.Sea-Monkeys: Sea-Monkeys are brine shrimp that hatch from dried eggs when you add water.

chapters.text: Name a knitting, crochet or sewing term

krillion.quip: A steek is a deliberate cut through finished knitting, used for Fair Isle cardigans.

quips.Frogging: Knitters call ripping out work 'frogging', because 'rip it, rip it' sounds like a frog.
quips.Kitchener stitch: Kitchener stitch grafts two live edges together so it looks like unbroken knitting.
quips.Amigurumi: Amigurumi is the Japanese art of crocheting or knitting small stuffed creatures.
quips.Selvage: A fabric's selvage is its self-finished edge; the word comes from 'self-edge'.

chapters.text: Name a magic trick or sleight of hand

krillion.quip: A Victorian glass-reflection illusion; Disney's Haunted Mansion ghosts still use it.

Rabbit out of a hat: Pulling a rabbit out of a hat
Walking through a wall: Walk through the Great Wall of China
Out of this world: Paul Curry's Out of This World

quips.Bullet catch: The bullet catch has claimed the lives of several performers over the centuries.
quips.Zig-zag girl: Robert Harbin's 1965 Zig Zag Girl slices a boxed assistant into three offset sections.
quips.Elmsley count: Alex Elmsley's count shows four cards as four while hiding the odd one out.
quips.Vanishing elephant: Houdini made a live elephant disappear on stage at New York's Hippodrome in 1918.

chapters.text: Name an art supply or technique

krillion.quip: Painters rest their brush hand on this stick to keep it steady for fine detail.

quips.Sfumato: Sfumato, Leonardo's smoky blending, comes from the Italian for 'vanished like smoke'.
quips.Pointillism: Pointillists like Seurat built images from tiny dots of pure colour.
quips.Trompe l'oeil: Trompe l'oeil is French for 'deceives the eye': painting made to look 3D.

krillion.quip: Germany's 'tree cake' is baked layer by layer on a spit, so slices show tree-like rings.

quips.Jaffa cake: A UK tax tribunal ruled in 1991 that Jaffa Cakes are cakes, not biscuits.
quips.Lamington: Lamingtons are Australian sponge squares dipped in chocolate and rolled in coconut.
quips.Battenberg: Battenberg's pink and yellow checkerboard is wrapped in marzipan.
quips.Panettone: Panettone is a tall Italian Christmas bread-cake studded with candied fruit and raisins.

chapters.text: Name something you'd find in a garage

krillion.quip: Mechanics lie on this low wheeled board to roll under cars.

quips.Creeper: Mechanics lie back on this low wheeled board to slide under cars.
quips.WD-40: WD-40 stands for 'Water Displacement, 40th attempt', the formula that finally worked.
quips.Axle stands: Never work under a car held up by a jack alone; axle stands keep it safe.

krillion.quip: The kerf is the slot a saw blade removes — it shares a root with 'carve'.

quips.Kerf: The kerf is the slot a saw blade removes — it shares a root with 'carve'.
quips.Birdsmouth: A birdsmouth is a V-notch cut in a rafter so it sits snugly on the wall plate.
quips.Spalting: Spalting is the dark lines fungi leave in wood; turners prize them.
quips.Dutchman: A Dutchman is a patch of wood glued into a damaged spot, shaped to match.

krillion.quip: Focus at this distance and everything from half of it to infinity looks sharp.

quips.Camera obscura: Latin for 'dark chamber', this pinhole-image idea is far older than photography.
quips.Bokeh: Bokeh comes from the Japanese 'boke', meaning blur or haze.
quips.Daguerreotype: The first practical photo process, announced in 1839, used a silvered copper plate.
quips.Sunny 16 rule: On a sunny day, set f/16 and a shutter speed of 1/ISO for a good exposure.

packs.name: Odds & Ends
packs.tagline: 21 rummages · the junk drawer of the deep

krillion.quip: Native sulfur crystallises bright yellow around volcanic vents and hot springs.

quips.Io: Jupiter's moon Io is splashed yellow by sulfur from its hundreds of volcanoes.
quips.Banana slug: Banana slugs grow up to 25 cm long, and many of them are bright yellow.
quips.22-spot ladybird: The 22-spot ladybird is lemon yellow and eats mildew instead of aphids.
quips.Brimstone butterfly: Brimstone butterflies hibernate as adults and can live for nearly a year.

krillion.quip: Marimo are living algae that curl into soft green balls and roll along lake beds.

quips.Sand dollar: A sand dollar is the flat, round skeleton of a burrowing sea urchin.
quips.Atomium: Brussels' Atomium is a 102 m model of an iron crystal in nine steel spheres.
quips.Puffball mushroom: A giant puffball can top a football in size and puff out trillions of spores.
quips.Moon jellyfish: A moon jelly's four pale horseshoe rings are its reproductive organs.

krillion.quip: Glyptodons were car-sized Ice Age relatives of armadillos in a domed bony shell.

quips.Armadillo: Armadillo is Spanish for 'little armoured one'.
quips.Geoduck: A geoduck's siphon is so long the clam can't fully pull it back into its shell.
quips.Horseshoe crab: Horseshoe crabs have blue blood and have been around longer than the dinosaurs.
quips.Coconut crab: Coconut crabs are the largest land arthropods and can crack coconuts with their claws.

krillion.quip: Sweden's nyckelharpa is a fiddle whose notes come from a row of wooden keys.

quips.Ophicleide: The ophicleide is a keyed brass instrument that the tuba later replaced.
quips.Hurdy-gurdy: A hurdy-gurdy makes its drone by cranking a rosined wheel against its strings.
quips.Calliope: A calliope is a steam-powered organ with a keyboard, heard at fairs and on riverboats.

chapters.text: Name something you'd find at the beach

krillion.quip: Those leathery black pouches on the shore are empty egg cases of skates or sharks.

quips.Sea glass: Sea glass is broken bottle glass tumbled smooth and frosted by years of waves.
quips.Cuttlebone: A cuttlefish's chalky cuttlebone is a gas-filled float, often sold for pet birds.
quips.Tombolo: A tombolo is a sandbar that links an island to the mainland.

chapters.text: Name something that runs on batteries

krillion.quip: A modern pacemaker's tiny lithium battery can power it for around ten years.

quips.Lunar Roving Vehicle: The Apollo moon buggy ran on non-rechargeable silver-zinc batteries.
quips.Sputnik 1: Sputnik 1's beeping radio ran on silver-zinc batteries that lasted about three weeks.
quips.Metronome: Mechanical metronomes use clockwork, but most modern ones run on batteries.

krillion.quip: Pumice is so full of gas bubbles that this volcanic rock floats on water.

quips.Fire ant raft: Fire ants link their bodies into a waterproof raft that can float for weeks.
quips.Sea otter: Sea otters hold paws while they sleep so they don't drift apart.
quips.Kon-Tiki: Thor Heyerdahl's 1947 balsa raft Kon-Tiki drifted 8,000 km across the Pacific.

krillion.quip: Hobbyists who hoard matchbooks and matchbox labels are called phillumenists.

quips.Fabergé eggs: Of the 50 imperial Fabergé eggs made for Russia's tsars, 43 survive today.
quips.First day covers: A first day cover is an envelope stamped on the very day a new stamp is issued.
quips.Netsuke: Netsuke are carved toggles once used to hang pouches from Japanese kimono sashes.
quips.Sugar packets: Collecting sugar packets is called sucrology.

krillion.quip: Sundew leaves glisten with sticky droplets that trap insects.

quips.Gecko feet: Gecko toes cling using tiny molecular forces, no goo required.
quips.Propolis: Propolis is the sticky resin bees collect to seal gaps in their hive.
quips.Butterwort: Butterwort leaves are slick with sticky mucilage that traps gnats.

chapters.text: Name something with teeth (not an animal)

krillion.quip: The little perforated edges around a postage stamp are literally called its teeth.

quips.Dragon's teeth: Dragon's teeth are rows of concrete pyramids built as tank barriers.
quips.Cog railway: Cog railways grip a toothed rack rail to climb slopes that adhesion trains can't.

krillion.quip: Hobby Tesla coils turn ordinary mains power into crackling, foot-long sparks.

quips.Theremin: A theremin is played without touching it, by moving your hands near two antennas.
quips.Van de Graaff generator: A Van de Graaff generator builds up static until your hair stands on end.
quips.Neon sign: Neon signs need a high-voltage transformer to light their glowing gas tubes.

krillion.quip: A bayan is a Russian chromatic button accordion, played by pressing rows of buttons.

quips.Telegraph key: A telegraph key is a spring-loaded button tapped to send Morse code.
quips.Snowman: A snowman's coal buttons are the classic finishing touch.

krillion.quip: Antarctica's Vostok Station recorded the coldest air temperature ever: -89.2°C.

quips.Boomerang Nebula: The Boomerang Nebula, at about 1 K, is the coldest known natural place in the universe.
quips.Oymyakon: Oymyakon in Siberia, the coldest permanently inhabited place, has hit about -67°C.
quips.Large Hadron Collider: The LHC's magnets run at 1.9 K, colder than the vacuum of outer space.
quips.Liquid helium: Liquid helium boils at about -269°C, colder than almost anything on Earth.

krillion.quip: Gallium melts at about 30°C, so a lump turns liquid in your warm hand.

quips.Wicked Witch of the West: The Wicked Witch of the West famously melts when Dorothy throws water on her.
quips.Dalí's melting clocks: Dalí's 1931 painting The Persistence of Memory made melting clocks famous.
quips.Cesium: Cesium melts at about 28°C, so it can turn liquid on a warm day.
quips.Wood's metal: Wood's metal melts at about 70°C, so a spoon of it dissolves in hot tea.

krillion.quip: A fish finder's screen paints sonar echoes into a picture of fish and seabed.

quips.Teleprompter: A teleprompter reflects scrolling text onto glass in front of a camera lens.
quips.Virtual Boy: Nintendo's 1995 Virtual Boy showed red-only 3D graphics and sold poorly.
quips.Game & Watch: Nintendo's Game & Watch handhelds put a tiny LCD game and a clock in one pocket gadget.

krillion.quip: NASA's BEAM module launched folded and inflated like a balloon on the space station.

quips.Barrage balloon: Barrage balloons were tethered over cities in WWII to snag low-flying aircraft.
quips.Echo 1 satellite: Echo 1 (1960) was a 30 m balloon satellite that bounced radio signals worldwide.
quips.Evacuation slide: Aircraft escape slides inflate in about six seconds when the door is opened.

chapters.text: Name something that comes in pairs

krillion.quip: Claves are two hardwood sticks, tapped together to keep Latin rhythm.

quips.Chromosomes: Humans carry 23 pairs of chromosomes in almost every cell.
quips.Cleopatra's Needles: Ancient Egyptian obelisks called Cleopatra's Needles stand in London and New York.
quips.Pillars of Hercules: The Pillars of Hercules are the rocks flanking the Strait of Gibraltar.

krillion.quip: The mizzenmast is the aft mast on a sailing ship, behind the main mast.

quips.Rizz: Rizz, short for charisma, was Oxford's 2023 Word of the Year.
quips.Gizzard: A gizzard is the muscular stomach birds use to grind food with swallowed grit.
quips.Muezzin: A muezzin is the person who gives the Islamic call to prayer.

chapters.text: Name a compound word starting with "sun"

krillion.quip: The sunbittern flashes sun-like eyespots on its spread wings to startle predators.

quips.Sundog: A sundog is a bright spot on either side of the Sun caused by ice crystals in the air.
quips.Sundew: Sundews are carnivorous plants named for the dew-like drops on their leaves.
quips.Sunquake: A sunquake is a burst of seismic waves rippling out through the Sun after a solar flare.

chapters.text: Name an animal with a three-letter name

krillion.quip: The kea is the world's only alpine parrot, and it loves to shred car rubber.

quips.Moa: The giant moa of New Zealand was a wingless bird up to 3.6 m tall, hunted to extinction.
quips.Ayu: The ayu is a Japanese sweetfish prized for its faint melon-like scent.
quips.Eft: An eft is the juvenile land stage of a newt.

krillion.quip: In 1854 John Snow had a Broad Street pump's handle removed to stop a cholera outbreak.

quips.Gavel: A gavel's handle lets a judge rap for order without hurting a hand.
quips.Dibber: A dibber is a pointed gardening tool, handle on top, for poking planting holes.
